#!/bin/bash

# WARNING: the following assumes that the variable "x" is not used in jsfxr() _after_ the Closure Compiler

# Compress JavaScript
java -jar compiler.jar --compilation_level ADVANCED_OPTIMIZATIONS --externs externs.js --js jsfxr.js | \
	tr -d '\n\r' |
	sed 's!"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789\+/"!x!g' | \
	sed 's!"data:audio/wav;base64,"!"data:audio/wav;base64,",x="ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/"!g' > jsfxr.min.js

# Check file size
wc -c jsfxr.min.js
slice_results.behavior_summary: When executed (shell script), the code runs the Closure Compiler on jsfxr.js to produce a minified JavaScript file, then processes the output by removing newlines and replacing base64 characters with a placeholder before writing the result to jsfxr.min.js, resulting in a compressed and obfuscated JavaScript file.
slice_results.explanation: [LLM Judgment: Benign] The provided script is a build/optimization script that uses the Closure Compiler to minify a JavaScript file (jsfxr.js), then performs some text processing to remove newlines and replace base64 characters with a placeholder before saving the output. This is a common practice in JavaScript build pipelines to reduce file size and obfuscate code for performance or intellectual property protection. There is no evidence of downloading or executing remote binaries, no network communication, no system manipulation beyond file processing, and no automated malicious payload distribution. The known malicious patterns involve downloading and executing remote binaries or mass publishing malicious packages, none of which are present here. The use of sed and tr for character replacement is benign in this context and does not indicate malicious intent.
